questions.q: A program that appears to be a free game but silently opens a backdoor for attackers is a:
questions.solution: The trojan's essence is disguise: useful-looking software that performs hidden malicious actions (backdoors, data theft). It does not self-replicate.
questions.shortcut: Looks useful, works evil = trojan horse.

questions.q: The browser shortcut to open a new tab is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+T opens a new tab; Ctrl+N a new window; Ctrl+W closes the current tab; Ctrl+Tab cycles through open tabs.
questions.shortcut: T = Tab, N = window. Ctrl+W wipes the tab.

questions.q: Which Office-wide shortcut opens the Font dialog box in PowerPoint?
questions.solution: Ctrl+T opens the Font dialog (face, style, size, effects) in PowerPoint. Ctrl+F is Find; Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide/object.
questions.shortcut: In PPT, T = Type(faces): Ctrl+T is the font box.

questions.q: Which shortcut minimises all open windows to show the desktop, and restores them when pressed again?
questions.solution: Win+D toggles the desktop: the first press hides every window and the second press brings them back. Win+E opens File Explorer, and Win+Tab/Alt+Tab switch windows.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A person appointed to hear both sides and settle a dispute
questions.solution: An **arbitrator** is the authorised settler of disputes. *Agitator* stirs trouble, *dictator* rules absolutely, *philanthropist* gives to charity — different families entirely.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: Nagpur is itself a city of Maharashtra, so it must not be compared with itself: harsher than **any other city** in Maharashtra.
questions.shortcut: member vs own group → any other.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The teacher has said, "The exam will begin at ten."
options: The teacher has said that the exam would begin at ten.
The teacher has said that the exam will begin at ten.
The teacher said that the exam will begin at ten.
The teacher has said that the exam will be begun at ten.
questions.solution: The present perfect frame **has said** is still a present reporting verb — no backshift: **will begin** stays. 'Would begin' applies a past-frame rule to a present frame; 'The teacher said' downgrades the frame; 'will be begun' pushes a future simple into a passive.
questions.shortcut: has said is present too — the ladder is not climbed.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Between you and I, / the newly appointed / manager has no / practical field experience.
questions.solution: A preposition takes object forms: *between you and **me***. *I* is a subject form and cannot follow *between*.
questions.shortcut: Preposition + I is always the error; flip it mentally: 'between me'.

questions.q: The **Partition of Bengal** (1905) was carried out by which Viceroy?
questions.solution: **Lord Curzon** announced the partition, which took effect on **16 October 1905** and triggered the Swadeshi movement. It was annulled in **1911** under Lord Hardinge.

questions.q: Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya as the ambassador of —
questions.solution: **Megasthenes** was sent by **Seleucus Nicator** after the treaty of 305 BCE and wrote ***Indica***. Deimachus came from **Antiochus I** to Bindusara's court.

questions.q: Vitamin K is essential for:
questions.solution: **Vitamin K** is needed to make clotting factors (such as prothrombin) in the liver; its deficiency leads to excessive bleeding. Vision needs vitamin A, gums need C, bones need D.

questions.q: The **Prayag Prashasti** inscribed on the Allahabad pillar, praising Samudragupta, was composed by —
questions.solution: **Harishena**, Samudragupta's court poet and minister, composed the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad pillar, which also carries Ashokan edicts). It lists Samudragupta's campaigns in the north and the south.

questions.q: In a workforce of 4,800, the pie chart shows two departments occupying 15% and 25% of the circle. The number of employees in these two departments together is:
questions.shortcut: Add the shares first: 40% of 4800 = 1920. One multiplication, not two.

questions.q: The value of $2(\sin^6\theta+\cos^6\theta)-3(\sin^4\theta+\cos^4\theta)+1$ is:
questions.shortcut: The $s^2c^2$ terms cancel exactly: $-6+6=0$ → answer 0 for every $\theta$. (Try $\theta=45^\circ$ to confirm.)

questions.q: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenditures in the ratio 3 : 2. If each saves ₹1,600, then B's expenditure is:
A invests ₹15,000 for the first 4 months of a year and ₹20,000 for the remaining 8 months. B invests ₹18,000 for the whole year. The ratio in which they share the profit is:
How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution: Lines through the apex = 5 inner lines + 2 sides = 7. Any two of them make one triangle on a base: C(7, 2) = (6 × 7)/2 = 21. Total = **21**.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**3   12**

**7   28**

**9   ?**
questions.solution: Second number = 4 × first: 3 × 4 = 12 ✓, 7 × 4 = 28 ✓. So 9 × 4 = **36**. (27 uses ×3, which fits neither row.)
questions.shortcut: Divide the output by the input — a constant quotient means a constant multiplier.

questions.q: Which word would a dictionary list **first**: Play, Player or Plays?
questions.solution: Play is a prefix of both Player and Plays, so it sorts before them → **Play** first.
questions.shortcut: Prefix beats extensions — no deeper comparison needed.

questions.q: **A is 7th from the left end and B is 19th from the left end of a row. How many people are between them?**
questions.solution: Same end: $|19 - 7| - 1$ = **11** people between.
questions.shortcut: Same-end gap minus the two named people.
